rows.reason: The failure assertions request the last populated test-fixture slot, while the RT writer copies payload and then increments RTBlockHeader::_size; _size is a plain uint32_t count, and the writer uses a process-local SpinMutex. The reader deliberately searches only [_ticks, _ticks + (_size - 1)] (equivalently other RT HFT collections), with a per-reader mutex that does not coordinate separate processes. Source evidence therefore shows copied-count intent and conservative tail exclusion, but does not establish a cross-process publication barrier or atomic payload snapshot. A static fixture expectation cannot prove reading the last live slot is safe. This is a separate ambiguity from BUG-R100-002 before-first eIdx underflow; keep BLOCKED until the visibility contract and cross-process synchronization are established.
remaining: Confirm whether RT HFT readers should observe the latest copied slot while the writer remains active, or whether one trailing slot is intentionally writer-owned.
If latest committed data must be visible, implement a documented cross-process publish protocol; if not, align the oracle to the documented contract only after the contract is confirmed.
Run deterministic separate-process producer/reader tests with an instrumented pause around publication, sequence/checksum validation, repeated range/count reads, and resize/remap coverage.
Do not attribute the other v5 storage failures to this issue without independent triage; the whole storage suite is not a pass.
